thread.title: Dow Jones Lags Nasdaq; Can This Sector Boost Stocks? | Investor's Business Daily

author: DAVID SAITO-CHUNG
title: Dow Jones Lags Nasdaq; Can This Sector Boost Stocks? | Investor's Business Daily
text:
The Nasdaq composite held a slim margin over other key indexes but remained significantly off session highs with a 0.2% slip. The Nasdaq 100, hampered by continued struggles by former market leader Apple, was flat. Volume was tracking lower on both main exchanges.
Meanwhile, a large portion of the IBD 50 shows numerous high-growth companies in the ethical drug, biotech, medical services and medical device industries. They include BioTelemetry ( BEAT ), Horizon Pharma ( HZNP ), Medpace ( MEDP ), dividend-rich CareTrust REIT ( CTRE ), Innoviva ( INVA ) and Charles River Labs ( CRL ). Many of these companies fall within small- and midcap territory.
Go to the IBD Weekly newspaper or the entire IBD 50 list at Investors.com to read an instant analysis of buy points, sell signals and chart action for each of these names.
New bull runs need fresh blood from a variety of sectors. Right now, business software is trying to re-emerge as a sector leader. On Tuesday, semiconductor stocks rallied sharply yet remain industry laggards overall.

Please contact customer service CLOSE The Dow Jones industrial average surrendered decent morning gains and fell 0.6%. Wall Street popped higher at the open on a Bloomberg report that noted the possibility of a Chinese cut in tariffs on imported cars to 15% from a current 40%. But the arrest of telecom gear and smartphone giant Huawei Technologies' CFO still hangs as a dark cloud over equities.
The S&P 500 gave up all of an early 1.3% advance to trade down 0.3%.
Market breadth improved, though.
Winners edged losers by a nearly 15-14 ratio on the Nasdaq, 6-to-5 on the NYSE.
In The Nasdaq: Apple Stock Profits Dwindle Apple ( AAPL ), trading as low as 163.33 earlier in the week, still commands a decent overall gain of 42% since it produced a solid breakout from a first-stage cup with handle back on Jan. 6, 2017. The proper buy point back then was 118.12. Now, however, shares have tumbled nearly 30% from an all-time high of 233.47.
This means that the major indexes will need to see new stock leaders with excellent or improving fundamentals to lead the next stock market uptrend, with brand-new breakouts from good bases to 52-week or all-time highs. Apple, meanwhile, has a ton of work ahead in crafting a potential new base.
A Medical Sector Leader Not In The Nasdaq Edwards Lifesciences ( EW ) rallied as much as 2.2% before surrendering most of that gain. The cardiovascular health technology expert has been forming the right side of a cup with handle that shows a 165.41 proper buy point.
Find the handle by adding 10 cents to the highest intraday price within the handle portion of the base. In this case, Edwards' handle began forming with a negative reversal on Dec. 3. The handle shows a price high of 165.31 and a gentle drift lower along the lows.
One could also interpret the daily or weekly chart action as a breakout from a smaller cup with handle and a 158.42 buy point. Nonetheless, the base itself shows a mild decline of 22%, which is bullish.
Notice on a daily chart how the relative strength line has recently made new highs, another bullish sign that's it's sharply outperforming the S&P 500.
On Stock Checkup , Edwards gets a high Composite Rating of 98 on a scale of 1 to 99. That ranks Edwards 3rd within the entire Medical-Products group.
This Gold Stock Still Glitters Kirkland Lake Gold ( KL ), which has shown up in the Stock Spotlight list in recent days, continued its breakout past a 23.96 buy point in a four-month cup without handle.
The Toronto-based explorer of golf and minerals has posted net profits every year since 2015, when it earned 8 cents a share. This year, the Street expects earnings of $1.15 a share, up 47% vs. 2017. Read more about the chart analysis of Kirkland Lake in this new Stock Spotlight column .
